metadata.description: Post-quantum cryptography reference — ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FN-DSA, hybrid TLS; harvest-now-decrypt-later threat; crypto inventory classes; readiness assessment

source: NIST FIPS 203/204/205/206, NSA CNSSP-15, IETF TLS hybrid drafts (summarized)

algorithmIndex.name: ML-KEM (Kyber)
algorithmIndex.type: KEM — key encapsulation (replaces RSA/ECDH key exchange)
algorithmIndex.status: Finalized Aug 2024. Deployed in Chrome/Edge TLS (X25519MLKEM768 hybrid) since 2023.

algorithmIndex.name: ML-DSA (Dilithium)
algorithmIndex.status: Finalized Aug 2024. Widely available in OpenSSL 3.5+.

models.detail: RSA-2048/3072, ECC P-256, ECDSA — breakable by 4096 logical qubits (Shor's algorithm on ~2M physical qubits for RSA-2048).
Classical + PQC combined (e.g. X25519MLKEM768, RSA + ML-DSA certs) — safe against HNDL today; smallest operational change.
ML-KEM/ML-DSA-only stacks — trust that lattice assumptions hold; required only when hybrid is unsupported (some hardware/HSM contexts).

hndl.summary: Adversaries (esp. nation-states) archive encrypted traffic today; when a quantum computer reaches thousands of logical qubits, they decrypt the archive in bulk — including data with a decades-long secrecy need (health records, PII, patents, defense comms).
timeline: NSA CNSSP-15: protect secret data by 2030, top-secret by 2033
NIST: PQC standards finalized 2024; migration recommended to start before 2030
Industry: hybrid TLS already ships (Chrome, Edge, Cloudflare, AWS KMS)
Conservative analysts: large-scale cryptanalytic quantum computer 2030–2035; 'store now, decrypt later' risk is real TODAY for 10+ year secrets
whoShouldActFirst: Anyone with data that must stay confidential >10 years
PKI operators, HSM-hold crypto inventory owners
mitigations: Adopt hybrid key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) on all TLS/SSH/messaging now
PQC for all NEW keys; classic→PQC transition for long-lived certs
Post-quantum signatures (ML-DSA/SLH-DSA) for certificate authorities & firmware
Inventory all crypto assets and classify by secrecy horizon — anything ≫10 years is HNDL-exposed
Monitor NIST/CNSA transition deadlines when selecting new products

cryptoClasses.action: Root and intermediate CAs re-key to ML-DSA (or SLH-DSA); issue PQC leaf certs; plan hybrid chains during transition.
Enable X25519MLKEM768 on servers/CDNs/clients; verify with SSL Labs 'Post-quantum' tag; hybrid-certs for mutual TLS.
sntrup761x25519-sha512 key exchange + ML-DSA host keys (OpenSSH 9.0+); port in inventory.
S/MIME with PQC-able CAs (2024 RSA-1024 ban raised cert churn); PGP keys remain quantum-vulnerable — plan re-key.
IPsec: enable hybrid PQC (post-quantum IKEv2 drafts); WireGuard: switch to PQ-hybrid WG keys when upstream ships.
Sign with ML-DSA or SLH-DSA; retain long-term verification chains; HSM support required.
At-rest AES-256 is quantum-safe (Grover halves to 128); key exchange protecting the keys is the PQC concern.
Already forward-secret sessions safe; HNDL risk is only non-FS flows (old RSA key transport).
Migrate zone-signing keys to FN-DSA/ML-DSA when validator/registrar support arrives; signature size matters.
Validate FIPS 140-3 modules shipping ML-KEM/ML-DSA; inventory module versions for key-migration readiness.

readiness.question: Do we have a complete crypto inventory (certificates, TLS configs, SSH keys, HSMs, signing keys)?
Is every TLS endpoint (incl. internal services, IoT, appliances) identified and versioned?
Have we classified data/communications by secrecy horizon (>10 years = HNDL-relevant)?
Are new certificates issued on PQC-capable CAs (ML-DSA hybrid chains)?
Is X25519MLKEM768 enabled on internet-facing servers/CDN?
Are remote-access VPNs and SSH configured with PQC-capable key exchange?
Do our HSMs/crypto modules support ML-KEM/ML-DSA (FIPS 140-3 validated)?
Is code/firmware signing migrated (or planned) to ML-DSA/SLH-DSA?
Have we identified vendor PQC adoption roadmaps for third-party products?
Is PQC migration tracked as a formal project with an owner and 2030 deadline?
Do we test hybrid key exchange in staging before production rollout?
Is DNSSEC / mail / document signing on the PQC plan (with sighsize impacts assessed)?
